gappers.catalyst: Phase 2 FREEDOM2-DM1 data at 10 mg/kg showed 46.5% mean splicing correction vs 6.8% for placebo, driving a near-doubling on Nov 10 that is extending today.
headlines: PepGen Shares Rise 92.9% After Phase 2 Myotonic Dystrophy Results (TokenPost)
Why Is Penny Stock PepGen (PEPG) Up 114% Today? (TipRanks)
PepGen Stock Soars Despite Wider Q3 Loss (RTTNews)
gappers.catalyst_detail: PepGen reported Phase 2 FREEDOM2-DM1 results in myotonic dystrophy type 1: the 10 mg/kg cohort delivered 46.5% mean splicing correction versus 6.8% on placebo, which the company calls the highest level reported in a multiple-dose study and Guggenheim flagged as a potential new benchmark for splicing. No serious or severe adverse events and no dose-limiting toxicities were reported, and cash of $104.8M at Sep 30 is guided to last into 2028. Offsetting that, PepGen simultaneously proposed a $125M public equity offering, an FDA partial clinical hold is still in force with no US participants dosed, and the 12.5 mg/kg cohort does not read out until 1H 2027. Q3 loss of $0.28/sh came in slightly wider than consensus but was immaterial next to the data.
gappers.why: Binary clinical readout on a lead asset in a rare-disease indication re-rates the whole equity at once: a sub-$5 stock with a credible best-in-class splicing result pulls in biotech momentum and short-covering flow, amplified by BofA's upgrade off underperform to neutral ($6 PT) and a Street consensus PT far above spot.
gappers.impact: Volume is the tell and it cuts against sustainability of the *second* leg: 105M shares traded on the Nov 10 event day against a tiny float, but only ~92K in premarket today, the thinnest of any name on this list. That is an extended third day with no fresh information, so today's +24% is momentum chasing an already-priced catalyst, not new demand. The $125M offering is a hard overhead supply event that typically caps post-data runs, and the partial clinical hold caps the ceiling until lifted. No sector read-through; this is idiosyncratic biotech and does not belong to the AI complex driving the rest of the board.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: The catalyst is real and structural for the asset, but the tradable move is 3 days old, an announced dilutive offering sits directly overhead, and biotech is not a favored sector in either the early- or mid-cycle row of the strategy's rotation table.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Nothing to displace on the book (0 open positions, $100,000 cash), so the real cost is the weekly budget: 0/3 trades used for the week of Nov 9, and the Nov 11 pre-market run already earmarked XLV (and XLP as alternate) for the Nov 12 market-open. Taking PEPG spends a scarce weekly slot on the one name here that contradicts the desk's own defensive-rotation call. R:R also fails the gate at a sane stop: the mandated 10% trailing stop sits at ~$5.15, so clearing 2:1 requires ~$6.87 (+20%) from an already +150%-in-two-days base, and a $125M offering overhead makes that the low-probability side of the trade. Research only, no size recommended.

gappers.catalyst: Q3 revenue rose 168% to ~$3.66B, beating consensus, with record ~$133B backlog and raised FY26 guidance.
headlines: CoreWeave (CRWV) Q3 earnings report 2026 (CNBC)
Revenue Surges 168% to $3.7 Billion as Backlog Hits Record $133 Billion (GuruFocus)
CoreWeave Q3 Revenue Surges 168% but Capex Soars to $14.5B (TradingKey)
gappers.catalyst_detail: CoreWeave reported Q3 on Nov 10: revenue ~$3.66B, up 168% y/y and ahead of the ~$3.55B consensus, with adjusted operating income of $379M against guidance of $200-260M. Revenue backlog/RPO hit a record ~$132.5-133B, up 138% y/y, and FY26 revenue guidance was raised to $13.0-13.3B against $12.86B consensus, with an exit run-rate of $20-21B. The offset is capital intensity and losses: net loss widened to $709M from $110M, Q3 capex was $14.5B and FY26 capex guidance is $37-39B. Management said it will not tap the unsecured debt market at current yields and pointed to ~$9B of expected customer prepayments and deposits over the next three months.
gappers.why: This print was the swing factor for the entire AI-infrastructure trade, not just for CoreWeave. The complex had been sold hard post-midterms on fears that hyperscaler commitments were softening; a beat-and-raise with a record backlog directly falsifies that thesis, so the stock gaps and the whole neocloud/data-center-power group gets re-marked with it.
gappers.impact: Most sustainable-looking move on the board. Premarket volume of ~577K is the second-heaviest here and the catalyst is a company-specific, contractually-backed fundamental reset rather than a headline, so this reads as repricing rather than a one-day spike. The sector read-through is explicit and visible across today's own list: NBIS +15%, BE +12.6%, ORCL +6.8% are all moving on this same print. The genuine risk is not the quarter but the funding model, with $37-39B capex, a widening loss and an unsecured market management itself calls unusable, meaning any credit or AI-capex wobble hits this name hardest and fastest.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: Raised guidance plus a 138%-y/y contracted backlog is a structural reset rather than a headline, and it sits in Technology, a favored early-cycle sector in the strategy's rotation table, so it merits a multi-day swing if it later clears the Confluence rule on a /trade check.
gappers.opportunity_cost: With 0 open positions there is no holding to displace, so this competes against today's own list and the already-queued defensive names. Of the five deep dives, this is the one whose catalyst best survives scrutiny, so taking it would most reasonably displace the XLV/XLP entry queued for Nov 12, and that is a genuine trade-off, not a free swap: it swaps a low-beta defensive for the highest-beta expression of AI capex, in a week where only 3 trades are allowed and 0 are used. R:R can clear 2:1 on paper, as the 10% trail sits at ~$52.77 and 2:1 needs ~$70.36, but entering a +20% gap means buying the top of the move, so a pullback entry toward the gap base is the only version of this that passes a sane stop distance. Research only, no size recommended.

gappers.catalyst: Sympathy rally on CoreWeave's Q3 beat easing AI-neocloud demand fears, one day ahead of Nebius' own Q3 report on Nov 12.
headlines: Why Is Nebius Group Stock Soaring Wednesday? (Benzinga)
Nebius and IREN Stocks Pop on CoreWeave's Q3 Earnings (TipRanks)
Neocloud Stocks Rally as CoreWeave Earnings Ease AI Infrastructure Concerns (GuruFocus)
gappers.catalyst_detail: Nebius has not reported yet; today's gap is pure read-through from CoreWeave's beat-and-raise, which eased fears about neocloud demand across the group. The move follows a sharp prior-session decline tied to concerns that Microsoft was scaling back its neocloud partnership with Nebius, so part of today's gap is the unwind of that specific fear rather than new information. Nebius reports Q3 on Nov 12, with consensus at ~$907.5M revenue, up from $146.1M a year earlier, and a loss of ~$0.69/sh. The company has reaffirmed FY26 revenue guidance of $3.0-3.4B and an annualized run-rate of $7-9B. The stock remains far below its $300 all-time high after the neocloud de-rating.
gappers.why: Highest-beta liquid proxy for the same AI-compute demand thesis CoreWeave just validated, so index and momentum flow reaches for it first. The mechanism is correlation, not company news: nothing about Nebius' own economics changed overnight.
gappers.impact: Reads as the least durable of the AI-complex gaps precisely because it is borrowed conviction. Premarket volume of ~265K is solid but the move is unsupported by any Nebius-specific disclosure, and the stock carries a binary event in under 24 hours. Buying a +15% sympathy gap directly into your own earnings print is taking the gap risk twice, and the unresolved Microsoft-partnership question is exactly what the Nov 12 call will address, in either direction. Sector read-through is the same CoreWeave-driven cohort as CRWV/BE/ORCL.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: The catalyst belongs to a different company and the durable information arrives tomorrow, so there is no own-name thesis to hold through, and the earnings event makes a stop meaningless overnight.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Taking NBIS here spends one of 3 weekly trade slots on the same factor exposure CRWV already offers, but one step removed from the actual catalyst and with an earnings gap in front of it. It would also likely trip the correlation gate against CRWV if that position existed, since the strategy blocks a new entry correlating >0.75 with 2+ open positions, and this entire cohort trades as one factor. Within today's list it is strictly dominated by CRWV, which has the real catalyst and no imminent event. R:R is not assessable at a sane stop: a 10% trail at ~$138.67 sits well inside a plausible post-earnings move, so the stop is likely to be gapped through rather than respected, which fails the 2:1 minimum on any honest reckoning. Research only, no size recommended.

gappers.catalyst: Data-center power demand continues to re-rate the name — 900 MW NTT DATA agreement and 702 MW for Google's $17B Wyoming campus — as it rebounds from the post-midterm selloff on CoreWeave's AI-capex validation.
headlines: Why Bloom Energy Stock Popped Today (Motley Fool)
Why is Bloom Energy stock surging today? (Investing.com)
Brookfield to invest $5 billion to deploy fuel cells at data centers (CoStar)
gappers.catalyst_detail: Bloom's move is a continuation rather than a single new headline. On Nov 5 it announced a 900 MW onsite power agreement with NTT DATA across multiple global data-center projects and a 702 MW role supplying fuel cells for Google's newly unveiled $17B Wyoming campus, on top of a Brookfield AI-infrastructure financing framework since expanded to $25B and a backlog reported around $25B. The stock then plunged roughly 22% in the two days after the midterm elections as the market repriced policy risk for data-center-exposed names, and has been recovering since, with a ~13% bounce on Nov 9 helped by an RBC Outperform reiteration at a $335 target. Today's gap extends that recovery on CoreWeave's confirmation that AI capex is not slowing. Note the quote: Alpaca's prev close of $185.45 is the authoritative reference, as press figures around $185-200 conflict across sources.
gappers.why: Bloom is the power bottleneck in the AI buildout, so it trades as a levered derivative of data-center capex. CoreWeave's record backlog and $37-39B capex guide is direct evidence that the megawatts Bloom sells are still being contracted, which reverses the post-election de-rating premise.
gappers.impact: Moderately sustainable, with the caveat that this is the third large directional swing in four sessions: -22% then +13% then +12.6% is a volatility regime, not a trend, and premarket volume of ~103K is light relative to the ~15M shares that traded on the Nov 9 bounce. The underlying contract flow is real and multi-year, but the day-to-day price is being set by AI sentiment and election-policy headlines rather than by order news. Read-through runs both to the AI complex above and to the broader power/industrial names.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: The 900 MW and 702 MW agreements plus a $25B Brookfield framework are structural, multi-year revenue, and Industrials is a favored early-cycle sector in the rotation table, though the entry timing is poor mid-swing.
gappers.opportunity_cost: At $208.74, the 20%-of-equity cap allows ~95 shares against $100,000 equity, so this is a full-size position competing directly with the queued XLV/XLP defensive entry for one of 3 weekly slots. It is also the same AI-capex factor as CRWV and NBIS, so pairing any two of them would concentrate the book in one theme and likely trip the correlation gate. The 2:1 test is the binding problem: a 10% trail sits at ~$187.87, which is below the Nov 10 close and inside the recent 22% swing range, so realized volatility is wide enough to stop the trade out on noise, and clearing 2:1 needs ~$250 (+20%). Waiting for the swing to settle is the better-priced version of this exposure. Research only, no size recommended.

gappers.catalyst: Q3 revenue more than doubled to $290.8M, bookings rose 112%, and the company set a 2027 adjusted EBITDA target of $125-140M with a pipeline above $16B.
headlines: Babcock & Wilcox Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript (Benzinga)
Reports Q3 2026 Earnings of $0.61 EPS and $290.8 Million Revenue, Surpassing Estimates (GuruFocus)
Babcock & Wilcox outlines 2027 adjusted EBITDA target of $125M-$140M while expanding pipeline beyond $16B (Seeking Alpha)
gappers.catalyst_detail: B&W reported Q3 on Nov 9: revenue of $290.8M against $139.2M a year earlier, adjusted EBITDA of $17.7M, and net income of $93.9M that includes a large non-cash warrant and stock-valuation gain. That gain explains the headline EPS conflict, with the company's release showing $0.61/sh while the AP snapshot reports $0.02/sh adjusted for non-recurring items, and the adjusted figure is the honest one. Bookings exceeded $228M, up 112% y/y, backlog stands at $2.5B, and the pipeline has expanded past $16B including 6 GW of incremental power-generation opportunity. Management repurchased $38M of shares and fully paid down its unsecured bonds, kept FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance at $80-105M, and set a 2027 target of $125-140M.
gappers.why: A sub-$5 balance-sheet-repair story levered to the same power-generation demand as Bloom: deleveraging plus a 112% bookings jump plus raised forward EBITDA converts a distressed equity into a going concern, and the small float means that re-rating moves the stock violently.
gappers.impact: Mixed and the most likely of the five to mean-revert. The operational improvement is genuine and the deleveraging is real, but the $93.9M net income is mostly a non-cash warrant gain rather than earnings, and quoted prices disagree sharply across sources ($3.76-$4.37 post-release), which signals a thin, erratic tape. Premarket volume of ~137K on a ~$5 stock is modest. Adjusted EBITDA of $17.7M against a $125-140M 2027 target means the forward number depends on execution not yet in the run rate. Power/industrial read-through aligns it with BE.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: The 2027 EBITDA reset is structurally meaningful, but at $4.96 with a thin tape, a non-cash-driven headline and a 2-day-old catalyst, this trades as a low-priced momentum vehicle rather than a thesis a stop can protect.
gappers.opportunity_cost: The binding constraint is quality rather than capital: with 0 positions and $100,000 cash, nothing is displaced, but spending one of 3 weekly slots on the lowest-priced, thinnest-tape name on the list is a poor use of the budget when CRWV offers a cleaner catalyst with real liquidity. The 2:1 test is the hardest failure of the five: a 10% trail at ~$4.46 is only ~$0.50 wide on a stock whose quoted price varies by more than that between data sources, so the stop is inside the noise, and clearing 2:1 requires ~$5.95 (+20%). Does not clear the gate at a sane stop distance. Research only, no size recommended.
